# Mission Canvas

> Custom software built around your business, with ongoing maintenance and agreed improvements. Start with one workflow and a clear scope of care.

Mission Canvas offers Customized Software as a Service: custom software built around a business workflow, with scoped maintenance and agreed improvements. Each engagement defines the build, costs, deployment and ongoing care. Book a workflow audit: https://pretendhome.github.io/audit/

Sound familiar?
Software shouldn't need a workaround for the workaround.
Every company has them.
The spreadsheet that fixes the CRM.
The manual check that keeps the process from going wrong.
The person everyone asks because the system doesn't tell them what to do.
It's easy to call this "just how we work." It isn't. It's what happens when the software stops matching the business.
We build around how you actually work, then maintain and improve the software as your business changes.
How it works

## We build it. Then we stay with it.
01 Audit 02 Redesign 03 Assemble 04 Operate

### Audit
Show us one recurring job: where it starts, who handles it and what gets in the way. Together, we choose the first useful scope. What you get
One workflow · A clear outcome Timing and ongoing care
We agree build timing once the scope is clear. Care covers the connections, fixes and improvements agreed for your workflow.

### Redesign
We agree what the software should do, which tools it connects and which decisions stay with your team. What you get
The steps, connections and review points Timing and ongoing care
We agree build timing once the scope is clear. Care covers the connections, fixes and improvements agreed for your workflow.

### Assemble
We build on a reusable foundation, then shape the software around your business. Your team reviews it using real examples and exceptions. What you get
Custom software · Reviewed with your team Timing and ongoing care
We agree build timing once the scope is clear. Care covers the connections, fixes and improvements agreed for your workflow.

### Operate
We maintain connections, fix problems and agree improvements as your business changes, with care scoped to the software you use. What you get
Maintained connections · Fixes · Improvements Timing and ongoing care
We agree build timing once the scope is clear. Care covers the connections, fixes and improvements agreed for your workflow.

## Questions.
What is Mission Canvas?
Customized Software as a Service: we build software for a recurring job in your business, then maintain it and make agreed improvements as the work changes. Who is it for?
Teams repeatedly chasing information, copying between tools or checking the same records. Client intake, document preparation and follow-up are useful jobs to discuss first. How is it different from a one-off software project?
We build on reusable foundations and stay responsible for ongoing care. Maintenance and agreed improvements continue after launch, with a team that knows the workflow. What happens in the audit?
Talk us through one recurring job: how it starts, the tools and people involved, and where it gets stuck. We identify a useful first outcome together. How long does it take?
The first walkthrough shows what needs connecting and building. We agree a delivery plan before work starts; maintenance and agreed improvements continue after the first release.

About Mission Canvas

# People who understand the work and build the software.
We bring operating, software and information-system experience to the same table. We start by listening to
the people who do the work.

## The team.

### Jason Covington
Fractional CFO, CPO and COO practice.

### Mical Neill
Twelve years in voice and knowledge systems.

### Daniele Mulas
IT, and making things useful to real people.

### Pierfrancesco Borghero
Running development teams.

## What we believe.

### Listen before building.
The people doing the job know where it gets stuck. We start with their tools, decisions and experience.

### Make the work understandable.
Your team should be able to follow what the software does, check its results and know when a person needs to decide.

### Stay with what we build.
Daily use teaches us what needs attention. Maintenance and agreed improvements keep that learning connected to the software.

## What we’re working toward.
These are outcomes we’re working to prove, not results we claim today.

### Give people their time back
Cut repetitive work, so attention goes to people, ideas and decisions.

### Make the work understandable
Help people follow the steps, check results and see where a decision came from.

### Connect what you know
Turn scattered information into something your team can search and share.

### Keep what people know
Capture how work is done before it leaves with someone who retires.

### Useful software for the team
Make the workflow usable by the people doing the job every day.

### Work better together
Let teams build, share and improve their workflows together.

### Earn trust
Privacy, security and human oversight first. Technology should earn trust, not demand it.

## Start with a job you know well.
Talk us through the request, report or recurring check your team handles every week. Show us where people
have to chase information or work around a tool.
Our role continues after launch: understand what happens in use, care for the software and agree what to improve next.

## Tell us about the job your team wants to work better.
Bring one recurring job. We’ll discuss what to build and how to keep it useful. Let’s talk

Download

# Explore the desktop tools.
Download an existing app to explore it. For software shaped around your business, we scope a custom workflow, its connections and ongoing care separately.

## Palette
Explore the desktop foundation with sample documents.
Mac Windows Linux

## Education
Explore the existing education desktop workspace.
Mac Windows Linux

## Logistics
Explore the existing logistics desktop workspace.
Mac Windows Linux Sample data

## Install the app you chose.
- Mac Open the.dmg and drag the app into Applications. Palette is signed and notarized.
If macOS still says the app can't be verified, right-click it and choose Open.
- Windows Run the -Setup.exe installer. It is not yet code-signed, so SmartScreen shows
"Windows protected your PC": click More info, then Run anyway.
- Linux Palette is a.deb: open it with your software installer, or run
sudo apt install ~/Downloads/MissionCanvas.deb. The other apps are.AppImage files,
which download without permission to run, so double-clicking does nothing. In a terminal, chmod +x
the file, then run it. On Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, first sudo apt install libfuse2. On Ubuntu 24.04 an
AppImage may quit at once with a "SUID sandbox" error; start it with --no-sandbox.
For developers

## Install the command line.
The command-line tool works with a repository or folder. Use its documentation to explore the developer setup;
custom business workflows and care are commissioned separately. Developer docs
macOS / Linux curl -fsSL https://missioncanvas.ai/install-cli.sh | sh
Windows irm https://missioncanvas.ai/install-cli.ps1 | iex

Construction and Real Estate

# Construction job costing and fleet software Keep the site and office on the same job.
Keep job records, delivery tickets and costs together so the site and office work from the same information.
We adapt Livella to your forms and maintain the agreed workflow.
Let’s talk Start with one workflow. Meet Livella

## From site records to office decisions.
Start with the parts that work today. We agree how your jobs, cost codes and forms fit, then maintain
the workflow as those needs change.
- 01

### Every job site in one record
Status, crews, documents and progress in one place. Each job’s costs run from estimate to actuals and stay current.
- 02

### Delivery tickets read by AI
Inbound and outbound delivery tickets are digitised, read automatically and tied to the right job.
- 03

### Safety and quality without paper
Protective equipment assignments and declarations in one record. Concrete pours and material quality logged for review.
- 04

### Fleet and fuel
Equipment records, due dates and job-site assignments. Fuel tracked by machine and by job. Scheduled maintenance and driver contracts linked.
- 05

### Crew and hiring
Employee records and roles without spreadsheets. AI screens résumés from application to shortlist.
- 06

### Office paperwork
Mileage reimbursements calculated and printed to PDF. Payments to vendors and employees ordered, tracked and approved. Invoices read automatically.
- 07

### An assistant that knows the business
Answers questions from the firm’s own data. Field notes can be dictated and transcribed automatically.
Meet Livella

## Livella
Job records, delivery tickets and costs, shared by the site and office.
Livella gives field teams and office staff a shared starting point. We agree the workflow, access and
ongoing care for your implementation.
Let’s talk Start with one workflow.
Runs every day at an Italian construction firm that pays for it and whose own work it was built around.

## Built with your crew. Kept useful as jobs change.
Start with one site-to-office workflow, then agree the work to keep it useful.

### Understand
We follow a site record into the office: who checks it, who retypes it and what holds up the job.

### Redesign
We agree how notes, delivery tickets and costs should reach the person who needs them.

### Assemble
We adapt Livella to your jobs, cost codes and forms, and check it with the people who use them.

### Operate
We maintain the agreed workflow as forms, jobs and office requirements change.

- Connected services and outside AI providers are identified in the scope.
- Access, export and support responsibilities are agreed before use. How we handle your data

Industries CV-01 Education

# Private AI for schools From a classroom note to a reviewed next step.
Teachers record observations and review parent drafts from the same student record. We adapt coursework and report formats, with care as those change.
Let’s talk Start with one workflow.

## What it handles today.
These parts work now. We adapt the forms, roles and review steps around a specific job, then agree their ongoing care.
- 01

### Student and class records
A learning profile for each student and each class that keeps growing across grades and teachers.
- 02

### Progress notes and IEPs
Review the notes extracted for each student before updating their record.
- 03

### Summaries for parents
A draft from confirmed records, for the teacher to review before sharing.
- 04

### Exercises from your coursework
Activities adapted from the school’s own coursework and textbooks, in three tiers.

## See the starting point.
An unedited product recording with sample data.
Education · recording ↑ Recorded 21 September 2026 on version 0.2.106, unedited: roster import, a report card into the lenses, an observation, a summary and a three-tier activity. The class is a sample.
Existing software to build on · Deployment agreed for your workflow · Scoped build and ongoing care
The underlying capabilities: 8 modules, 42 features
- M-01 Students A lens per student, built from what the school already writes down.
- M-02 Observe A short note, attached to the right child, in under a minute.
- M-03 Assess Language work reviewed, not graded by a machine.
- M-04 Prepare and Plan Lessons from the coursework the teacher already has.
- M-05 Summaries What goes home is checked before it goes.
- M-06 Ask Questions answered on the machine, and it says so.
- M-07 Governance and privacy The verdict is computed from the log, not asserted.
- M-08 Coordinator views The school, seen across classrooms.

Industries CV-04 Events & Venues

# Ticketing and access control software for venues Give venue teams one record from sale to gate.
Online sales, box office and entry share the same tickets. Care follows changes to your forms, gate rules and reports.
Let’s talk Start with one workflow.

## What it handles today.
These parts work now. We adapt the forms, roles and review steps around a specific job, then agree their ongoing care.
- 01

### Tickets
A sale issues the right ticket once, ready for staff to check at the gate.
- 02

### The gate
Gate staff see the decision and reason for each scan.
- 03

### The box office
Online and walk-up sales share a catalogue; shift staff reconcile the cash.

## See the starting point.
Interface schematics with illustrative data. Product screenshots will replace them.

- M-03 Venues and locations Sell on a place, not only on a date.
- M-04 Catalogue Products, add-ons, stock and tax.
- M-05 Checkout A configurable point of sale, online or in store.
- M-06 Form engine Structured data collection, versioned and reusable.
- M-07 Orders Three channels, one authoritative quote.
- M-08 Payments Stripe as the source of truth, fees included.
- M-09 Ticketing Typed tickets, issued once.
- M-10 Check-in A complete decision at every gate.
- M-11 POS The box office, with a cash drawer that adds up.
- M-12 Contacts and CRM A CRM fed by the sale itself.
- M-13 Profiling Know your visitors without writing code.
- M-14 Notifications and automations An event bus you can build on.
- M-15 Tenant administration Everything an operator needs to run their own house.

Questions

# Questions before we start.
What the service involves, what your team brings and what happens after launch. Bring any other questions to our first conversation.

## The basics
What is Mission Canvas?
Customized Software as a Service: we build software for a recurring job in your business, then maintain it and make agreed improvements as the work changes. Who is it for?
Teams repeatedly chasing information, copying between tools or checking the same records. Client intake, document preparation and follow-up are useful jobs to discuss first. How is it different from a one-off software project?
We build on reusable foundations and stay responsible for ongoing care. Maintenance and agreed improvements continue after launch, with a team that knows the workflow. What happens in the audit?
Talk us through one recurring job: how it starts, the tools and people involved, and where it gets stuck. We identify a useful first outcome together. How long does it take?
The first walkthrough shows what needs connecting and building. We agree a delivery plan before work starts; maintenance and agreed improvements continue after the first release. What is a canvas?
An industry starting point for a custom workflow. We use reusable building blocks and adapt the steps, rules and connections to your business.

## Cost and ownership
What does it cost?
An initial setup and build, followed by recurring care. Your quote explains the work included and any separate hosting, third-party or usage costs. Who owns what you build?
We make ownership, licensing and access clear before the build, including how the reusable foundation and your custom work are treated. What if we stop working together?
We agree how data can be exported, what is handed over and who will operate the software and its connected services.

## Your data and your systems
Does our data leave our computers?
We agree where the software runs, who can access the information and which connected services receive it before connecting your business data. Do we need new hardware?
We look at the equipment and systems you already use, then explain what the workflow needs before you decide to build. Can we keep the tools we use today?
We start there. We check how your tools can connect, what access they allow and where a person still needs to take the next step. What is Palette?
A separate desktop application for working with your files. Downloading Palette does not include a custom workflow build or the ongoing service described here.

## Let’s make one workflow work better.
Bring one recurring job. We’ll discuss what to build and how to keep it useful. Let’s talk
Start with one workflow.

How it works

# Start with one job. Make it work better.
Show us a recurring job, the tools involved and where the handoffs get difficult. We build around that work, review it with your team and keep improving it.
Let’s talk Start with one workflow.

## From your information to useful work
01 Read 02 Sort 03 Connect 04 Work

### Start with the information you use.
We identify the files, records and system connections this job needs. You choose what the software can access. What you get
The sources your workflow needs

### Pick out what the job needs.
We define the details the workflow depends on, including what to do when information is missing, outdated or conflicting. What you get
The details needed for the next step

### Bring the right records together.
We connect the relevant records and tools around this workflow, so people can follow the work without piecing it together by hand. What you get
Information connected around one job

### Review it on real examples.
Your team checks the software against everyday work and difficult cases. Then care keeps the connections working and improvements moving. What you get
Reviewed software for your team’s work
Working with us

## One workflow, from first scope to daily use.
We start with your workflow and reuse common capabilities so the build does not begin from scratch.
Your business rules, connections and review steps shape the software. Care keeps it useful as those needs change.

### Audit
Show us one recurring job: where it starts, who handles it and what gets in the way. Together, we choose the first useful scope.
You get One workflow · A clear outcome

### Redesign
We agree what the software should do, which tools it connects and which decisions stay with your team.
You get The steps, connections and review points

### Assemble
We build on a reusable foundation, then shape the software around your business. Your team reviews it using real examples and exceptions.
You get Custom software · Reviewed with your team

### Operate
We maintain connections, fix problems and agree improvements as your business changes, with care scoped to the software you use.
You get Maintained connections · Fixes · Improvements
Then the AI goes to work

## Ask it about your work. It answers from your records.
One real exchange in the existing Logistics build, on sample orders. It shows a starting point we can shape
around your workflow, with the care and improvements agreed for your business.
01 Ask in plain words "Where is REF-7100?" The answer gives the stage, owner, carrier and tracking number, with the records it came from listed underneath. 02 It keeps the thread "Tell me about them," then "show their late orders." Customer data is marked local-only on every answer. 03 It says no when it should A question it cannot classify gets "unknown", stays on the machine, and is blocked from going to an outside model.

Mission Canvas Palette

# The free desktop application: Palette
Explore the foundation. Try one folder.
Explore a folder, review the sources and see how document changes are recorded. Palette is a free desktop
tool; a custom business workflow and ongoing care are commissioned separately.
Mac Windows Linux
Palette runs on a computer.
Send yourself this page
and open it there.
Free. No account. Version 0.4.1, released 15 October 2026. Mac is signed and notarised. Windows is not yet
signed, so SmartScreen will warn you once: what to click, and how to check the file.
The design we are building toward. The app as it ships today is below, screen by screen.
See it work · 105 seconds, unedited

## Ask, change, read it back.
One take on the sample notes: a spoken request finds nineteen facts and the document appears; a spoken change and
a clicked one each become a new version; then it reads the document aloud in a voice that runs on the machine.
Recorded 21 September 2026 on a build of 0.3.8 with the two changes that shipped in 0.3.9: the note bar sits at
the bottom, and spoken requests apply without a confirm card.
Download the recording, 5 MB
What the walkthrough shows
See how selected information becomes a document, how its sources remain visible and how changes are recorded.
- 01

### Chosen folders.
The sample works with the folder you grant. It gives you a focused way to explore documents and their supporting sources.
- 02

### Permission before reading.
The preview lists a folder before its contents are read. The walkthrough shows the grant that allows reading to begin.
- 03

### Source-based documents.
The sample fills a fixed document layout from accepted facts. Use its source view to check the information behind a claim.
- 04

### Visible changes.
The walkthrough shows the information being kept and the document versions created as values change, with review behavior shown on screen.
- 05

### A sample without a model.
The sample document workflow runs without an AI model installed or a model key. That behavior is identified in the app.
- 06

### Recorded connections.
The app has a connection record you can inspect. The recorded sample ends with no external connections listed.
The first five minutes · screens from version 0.3.7, not drawings

## Follow the recorded document walkthrough.
These screens show version 0.3.7 running the sample notes. They document that walkthrough; later builds may
look or behave differently. Use the current app's screens and guidance to check the work you want to try.
- 01 Start with invented sample notes The walkthrough starts with four invented notes in the app’s own folder. They let you explore a small document workflow before choosing any of your own material.
- 02 Preview a folder before reading The preview shows names and counts, with the files it would read or skip. Reading the contents follows the folder grant.
- 03 Review the extracted facts The pictured build holds extracted facts on a card. Later Home behavior keeps requested facts in the same turn and lists them on screen.
- 04 Build from the accepted facts The pictured document uses a fixed template filled with accepted facts. Its panel records that no model wrote this draft.
- 05 Follow a claim back to its source The walkthrough shows claims beside the source words and files they came from, so you can check the supporting information.
- 06 Change a value and keep the history The pictured edit creates another document version while retaining the earlier one. The walkthrough shows the change and its review step.

Install · version 0.4.1 · 15 October 2026
- Mac
Open MissionCanvas.dmg and drag the app into Applications. It is signed and notarised. If macOS still says it cannot be verified, right-click the app and choose Open. Download for Mac, 683 MB
- Windows
Run MissionCanvas-Setup.exe. The installer is not yet code-signed, so SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC”. Click More info, then Run anyway. If you would rather check the file first, its SHA-256 is below. Download for Windows, 637 MB
- Linux
Open MissionCanvas.deb with your software installer, or run sudo apt install ~/Downloads/MissionCanvas.deb. Download for Linux, 701 MB
The files are still named MissionCanvas. They are Palette. SHA-256: check the file you downloaded

## About Mission Canvas
Mission Canvas builds software around recurring work in small and mid-sized businesses. It uses reusable
building blocks, adapts the workflow to the business, and provides ongoing maintenance and agreed
improvements. The company calls this Customized Software as a Service, or CSaaS.

# A clear build. A clear care plan.
A quoted build, followed by recurring care for connections, fixes and agreed improvements. We price both around your workflow.

## Define the job

## Setup and build
Quoted for your workflow
Custom software shaped around your business rules, built on a reusable foundation and reviewed using real examples.
- 3

## Ongoing care
Recurring, agreed by quote
Maintain connections, fix problems and make agreed improvements. The care plan explains what is included and how larger changes are priced.
- A defined first build
- Care with a clear boundary
- Outside services costed separately
- Larger changes quoted first

## Choose who will build it and keep it useful.

### Build in-house
Your team builds the software and takes responsibility for its connections, maintenance and future changes.

### Choose a product
Use an existing product when its features and configuration fit the work your team needs to do.

### Build with us
One team to shape the workflow, build the software and keep improving it, with a defined scope for the build and care.
The proposed model pairs a focused build with recurring care. Hosting, model usage and third-party subscriptions
are separate unless included in your quote. You see what is covered before we begin.

## Questions about cost.
What does it cost?
An initial setup and build, followed by recurring care. Your quote explains the work included and any separate hosting, third-party or usage costs. Who owns what you build?
We make ownership, licensing and access clear before the build, including how the reusable foundation and your custom work are treated. What if we stop working together?
We agree how data can be exported, what is handed over and who will operate the software and its connected services.

Last updated October 23, 2026 · Draft

# Your data, in plain words.
Here is what happens when you contact us through this website. Before connecting a custom workflow, we also
agree how it will use your business information.

## What this website collects
- No form submission to this site. The enquiry forms prepare a message in your email app for you
to review and send. We receive it only when you send it.
- No cookies or site analytics. This website sets no cookies and runs no analytics today.
Hosting and email providers may keep technical logs under their own policies.
- Arranging a time. The calendar is a preview until booking is configured. Use email to arrange
a conversation; choosing a preview slot does not confirm a meeting.

## Why we collect it
Only to discuss your workflow, arrange a conversation and follow up about it. We don't sell it, rent it or use it for
advertising.

## Connecting your email
If a workflow uses email, we start with your provider, such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or an IMAP
and SMTP service. We agree what the application can access and who will maintain the connection before
using it.

## How our software handles your business files
- We agree where the software runs and which files it can access.
- We identify any outside AI provider and what information it may receive before use.
- We make clear who can access information during maintenance and what records are kept.

Your data

# Know what it can see and do.
A useful workflow needs the right information and clear limits. Together, we decide what the software can access, where it runs and which actions need your team's review.
Your data

## The right information. A clear boundary.
Start with the information one workflow needs. Make its sources, access and actions clear, then keep those
choices visible as the software changes.

### Read
Choose the sources.
Use the selected files, records and exports this workflow needs, with access agreed before use.

### Sort
Keep the relevant details in view.
Define the information needed for the job and how to handle missing, conflicting or outdated records.

### Connect
Link records for this job.
Agree which systems exchange information, what each connection is for and which accounts it uses.

### Work
Keep important decisions with people.
Define what the software prepares or changes, which actions need review and what is recorded afterward.

### Know where it runs
Choose the processing and hosting arrangement for the workflow, including any outside services it needs.

### Control what it uses
Agree who can access the information and how permissions change when a person or role changes.

### Review important actions
Make sending, updating and other consequential actions clear, with the review and records your team needs.

### Maintain the boundaries
Care includes agreed support access and review of changes that affect information, permissions or connected services.
Keep these choices clear as the software changes
Your team should know which records support the work, who can access them and where they are processed. We make those choices part of the workflow. Information and access
Keeping the software useful means maintaining connections and fixing problems. We agree support access and
review changes that affect how your team's information is handled.
Maintenance and changes
Our foundation includes source references, version history and recorded actions. We check the workflow against
your examples, including missing information, revoked access and uncertain results.

## Your information and connected systems.
Does our data leave our computers?
We agree where the software runs, who can access the information and which connected services receive it before connecting your business data. Do we need new hardware?
We look at the equipment and systems you already use, then explain what the workflow needs before you decide to build. Can we keep the tools we use today?
We start there. We check how your tools can connect, what access they allow and where a person still needs to take the next step.
For information about details shared through this website, read the privacy page.

What is Mission Canvas

# Custom software. A team responsible for it.
Mission Canvas builds software for a recurring business workflow and stays responsible for its care.
That is Customized Software as a Service, or CSaaS.

## How the service fits together.
- 01

### One recurring job
Show us how it starts, what people need to decide and what a finished result looks like.
- 02

### Software that fits
We reuse common building blocks and tailor the steps, rules and connections to your business.
- 03

### A team to care for it
Maintenance, fixes and agreed improvements continue after launch, with someone responsible for keeping the workflow useful.

## What changes for your team.

### Less chasing
Bring the steps and records for one job together, so people can see what is ready and what needs attention.

### Your rules in the work
Build in the checks, decisions and approvals your team needs to reach a useful result.

### Room to change
As the process evolves, we review feedback with your team and agree the next improvement.

## Who it is for.
For teams chasing the same information across email, documents and systems. Find a familiar job in these industry starting points.
‹
- CV-05 In progress Construction & Real Estate Bring site records, delivery tickets and office decisions together.
- CV-01 Education Help teachers review student notes, lessons and parent drafts.
- CV-02 Logistics Give operations one view of stalled orders and the next customer update.
- CV-03 Voice & Front Desk Handle routine bookings and pass the right calls to staff.
- CV-04 Events & Venues Keep the box office and gate working from the same ticket records.
- CV-06 In progress Healthcare Plan clearer check-in and scheduling handoffs for clinic staff.
- CV-07 In progress Office & Administration Prepare invoices and repeat requests for the next reviewer.
- CV-08 Everything else Show us the recurring job your team wants to work better. ›

Why Mission Canvas

# The work changes. Someone should care for the software.
A working application still needs attention. Connections change, problems appear and your team finds better
ways to work. Our service keeps responsibility for that care alongside the build.

## The workaround becomes routine
Someone keeps copying information between tools because the process has no better way through.

## A connected tool changes
An update, a new field or a changed permission can affect the job your team relies on.

## The process moves on
New people, rules and customers change what the software needs to do.

## Find the right fit for the work.
Question Existing software Mission Canvas
What shapes the workflow The features and options available in the product The recurring job your team needs to complete
How you pay The product’s licence and support terms An initial build, followed by ongoing care
What changes Updates and configuration the product offers Improvements chosen around your workflow
When it fits Its existing features cover the job well Your team needs the steps and connections to work differently

## What ongoing care pays for.
The build gets the workflow working. Ongoing care covers the maintenance, support and agreed improvements
that keep it useful. See how we price that work on the pricing page.

## Care for the whole workflow.

### Keep connections working
Maintain the links between your workflow and the tools it uses, including the access those connections need.

### Keep results checkable
Use examples from the job to review a change before your team relies on it.

### Keep the knowledge
Record setup and operating steps so maintenance and handover can follow the work, rather than depend on memory. Read how we handle your data

## Start small. Keep learning.
Who it serves: teams with a recurring job that takes too much chasing, copying or checking.
How it works: build a useful first workflow, learn from its use and improve it together.
A focused start
Choose one recurring job and the result your team needs from it.
Reusable building blocks
Use common capabilities as a foundation, then fit the workflow to your business.
Someone responsible
Keep maintenance and support with a team that understands how the work runs.
A way to improve
Turn feedback from daily use into the next agreed change.
A useful first workflow · Someone to maintain it · A way to improve it
The build and ongoing service are priced for the work involved.
